\Delta & \Phi & 0 & 0 \\
0 & 0 & \Psi & \Delta^{\text{t}} \\
0 & 0 & \Theta & \Lambda^{\text{t}} \\
\end{pmatrix}
\]
where $\Lambda\in\text{Sp}(r)$, $\Psi\in\text{Sp}(s)$, $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are conjugate to $\Lambda$ and $\Psi$ respectively, $\Delta\in\text{Sp}(r,s)$, $\Theta\in\text{Sp}(s,r)$

A detailed investigation of the conventional Nambu-Goldstone theorem reveals that its applicability extends beyond the framework of a symmetric spontaneous symmetry breaking scenario. In fact, the theorem can be reliably applied in cases where a symmetry is partially broken, provided that the associated annihilation operator encompasses a linear combination of long-lived modes. A manifestly covariant Wigner function serves as a pivotal tool in identifying the long-lived Nambu-Goldstone bosons that arise from a partial symmetry breaking. The unusual Nambu-Goldstone theorem can be viewed as a variant of its conventional counterpart, characterized by the presence of a linear dispersion relation among the mode frequencies. The study of a $(d+1)$-dimensional Abelian Higgs model serves as a concrete example to illustrate the unusual Nambu-Goldstone theorem in both its relativistic and nonrelativistic forms.

Our proposed task, phrasal counterfactual generation, aims to produce grammatically correct sentences where a specified word or phrase has a different meaning. Our research introduces the DISCO corpus, a 100,000 sentence collection with corresponding replacement words or phrases, enabling various counterfactual generation evaluations. We outline a simple replacement approach and a more sophisticated method utilizing semantic roles and word senses, also designing the BART-Based Discrete Counterfactual Generation task to evaluate counterfactual generation through contextual priming. We utilize the BART-Based method to establish baseline performance indicators and examine the impact of various counterfactual generation constraints.

Research into epitaxial growth on two-dimensional surfaces is gaining momentum and a comprehensive understanding of this equilibrium is crucial. This study investigates the equilibrium between remote, pinhole, and van der Waals epitaxy of Mn$_3$Si$_{1.7}$Se films deposited on a graphene/sapphire substrate. A variety of techniques including X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, and transmission electron microscopy were utilized to examine the films. It is demonstrated that a long-range interaction between the sapphire and the film leads to a 30-degree misfit dislocation array and a 110 nm lateral spacing between epitaxially connected domains. Conversely, small defects on the graphene surface facilitate direct contact and van der Waals epitaxy. A threshold defect density is observed, below which the films exhibit a crystalline structure and ferromagnetism. This study highlights the significance of controlling defects on a two-dimensional growth surface to achieve desired long-range interactions and properties in the film.

A code is termed $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-linear if there exists a code of length $N$ that is invariant under the ring $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$ and forms a submodule of rank $k$ in the free module of rank $N$ over $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$. The task of identifying all such codes that have a given dimension $k$ can be broken down into an initial stage of determining the basic codes of rank $k$ and then the set of $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-linear codes of that particular dimension, which arises as the module generated by the former for all possible subsets of indices. The article at hand focuses on establishing a connection between these codes and those of $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$-linear, providing a method to obtain the former from the latter by applying an automorphism defined by a specific matrix. Furthermore, it is demonstrated how this relationship can be utilized to derive the parameters of the $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-linear codes of a specific dimension $k$ from those of the $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$-linear codes of the same dimension, and vice versa.

Deep neural networks with multi-label output structures have difficulty being utilized in practice due to excessive computation and memory requirements. This issue is compounded when working with large datasets. Researchers have resorted to reducing labels to binary or selecting a single primary label, often using collaborative learning methods. This study addresses a related problem where a model trained on single labeled data is used to extract multiple relevant labels. A novel approach, dubbed Multi-Label Instance Extraction (MLIE), is introduced to rectify this situation. MLIE identifies the most pertinent additional labels for each instance. To effectively train the model, a loss function is created that focuses on instance-specific labels. This results in a framework that leverages single labeled data for multi-label information. Experiments conducted on real-world datasets demonstrate MLIE's efficacy, showing that models can accurately determine multiple relevant labels for each instance with only single labeled data.

Quantum systems can be modeled using Hilbert spaces, which provide a framework for computing physical properties. However, in actual experiments, various technical issues can arise, influencing the status of measurements. Dirac's approach aims to balance the abstract, computable aspects of physical theories with the concrete, measurable outcomes. We have discovered that there is a sophisticated relationship between the world of statuses, defined as functions mapping observables to their corresponding values, and the realm of Hilbert spaces. This connection is reflected in a specific type of mathematical connection called a strong adjunction, which applies within a complex framework known as 2-categories. This adjunction governs how statuses can be derived from the structure of a system described within a Hilbert space framework. Additionally, it ensures that the physical properties of a system remain consistent across different descriptions.

The exact cause of gamma-ray acceleration in powerful radio galaxies remains a mystery. Although proton-proton collisions in jets can explain high-energy particle production, they fail to account for magnetic field strengths as reported in some galaxies. An alternative hypothesis involving the capture of a disk in the black hole can provide the necessary magnetic field and allow for particle acceleration through the combination of electromagnetic and relativistic forces in the jet's throat. This hypothesis is particularly effective for low-power radio galaxies with a particular type, being archetypal FRIs. For the classic BL Lac objects, a variant model is proposed that incorporates an electron-positron pair wind accelerating in the jet throat, yielding similar results. This model for high-powered jets is then applied to some prominent gamma-ray bright candidates, including 3C 264, PG 1302-103, and 3C 70, as well as the persistently active narrow-line radio galaxy, NLRG J020827-4440.4.

Early detection of heart conditions is crucial, and point-of-care methods like cardiac auscultation are vital for this purpose.  However, accurate abnormality detection from heart sounds obtained through auscultation is hampered by background noise and operator technique variability.  This study addresses these challenges by developing an effective method for assessing heart sound samples based on their structural content.  A novel approach is proposed that combines signal processing and geometry analysis techniques to describe the acoustic signal's semantic content.  This content-based representation ignores the signal's temporal characteristics, making it invariant to noise levels and recording technique.  Additionally, a feature extraction algorithm is introduced that leverages geometric properties of heart sounds to create compact, noise-resistant representations.  These representations can be used in machine learning-based classifiers, enabling the detection of heart conditions even in noisy recordings.  The proposed method's effectiveness is demonstrated through noise resilience testing and comparison with conventional signal processing-based approaches, as well as validation in noise-free recordings.  The results show that the proposed content-based method outperforms conventional signal processing methods, achieving accuracy rates of 90\% in noise-free recordings and 80\% in recordings with background noise.

The proliferation of wearable devices for health monitoring has resulted in vast amounts of data, enabling effective machine learning-based applications such as activity recognition, sleep staging, and fall detection. However, training accurate models using wearable data at a individual level is challenging due to limited data available for each person, a problem common in situations outside wearable health data. This paper addresses this issue by developing FedHealth, a federated transfer learning framework for wearable medical applications. FedHealth combines the benefits of federated learning and transfer learning to train a global model using data from multiple users. It leverages a strategic participation approach, ensuring that each participant securely contributes their data for model development while maintaining confidentiality. Experiments conducted using raw open data for activity recognition tasks showed a 8.6% average increase in accuracy using FedHealth over a baseline model. Additionally, evaluations using actual wearable data from 10 participants demonstrated a 20.8% average increase in accuracy.

This study compares and contrasts various approaches to portfolio optimization, focusing on the mean-variance method, entropy-based methods, extreme value theory, and stochastic programming. The study's initial section reviews these methods' underlying assumptions, theoretical foundations, and key variables. The second section explores the connection between these methods, citing examples and research that demonstrate relationships and contrasts. The study aims to provide a clear understanding of the connection between these methods, as well as opportunities for integrating them into a single framework.

The RisingCost project aims to simplify the integration of new applications, services, and tools in an enterprise setting by automating routine operational tasks and streamlining deployments. This approach, which we call Automated Software Processing (ASP), enables enterprises to rapidly incorporate the latest software technologies into their infrastructure. In return for this increased flexibility, the ASP framework expects unwavering trust in the developers and software systems it represents, trusting code, and system configurations. To demonstrate the practical potential of ASP, we developed a prototype ASP system for processing Linux applications and used it to integrate multiple current applications. Notably, we processed Firefox-3.0 in approximately 6 hours, from starting the build process to having an up-and-running production system with the current version of Firefox.

This paper examines a stochastic control problem where the cost function has jumping components and is subject to certain constraints. We aim to explore strategies that minimize expenses under uncertainty, with the ability to trigger sudden changes in costs for added benefits. Key results involve proving the existence of optimal control policies and detailing their characteristics. Furthermore, we establish the connection between our problem and a system of partial differential equations featuring a gap option.

A recent paper proposes an innovative concept where leptoquark pairs are created with disparate masses in high-energy proton-proton collisions. This uneven scenario can arise in certain theories beyond the standard model that leverage a specific symmetry called "neutrino tribology". By examining whether even or odd numbers of leptoquark particles participate in interactions, this model can influence how two leptoquark particles behave when they collide. Even though this model features only two main leptoquark variants, it can be expanded to include more, nonetheless requiring additional symmetry constraints. A comprehensive investigation is conducted into how this model relates to existing research, followed by a thorough analysis of the predicted outcomes for specific processes. This analysis reveals that even small differences in mass can significantly impact processes involving three leptoquark particles, whereas processes involving two leptoquark particles are largely unaffected. Even though the proposed model can generate distinctive signatures in high-energy collisions, it also faces challenges in providing a comprehensive explanation for certain phenomena beyond the standard model, notably the anomalous magnetic moment of the neutrino and certain rare particle decays.

A new factor that may affect the molecular gas temperature estimation comes from the assumption that gas is in thermal equilibrium, which may not always hold, especially in cases where the gas is subthermal. A previous study found that even in subthermal situations, CO emission still provides reliable temperature estimates, although with some bias. Here we examine the relationship between CO and C I lines in low-mass star-forming galaxies with varying levels of star formation activity. A comparison of C I and CO line ratios reveals a decrease in the ratio as the level of star formation increases, which can be attributed to the higher temperature of the molecular gas in more actively star-forming galaxies. This trend is more pronounced in a sample of ultra-luminous infrared galaxies (ULIRGs). The larger C I line width compared to CO in both types of galaxies may indicate higher turbulent velocities and larger reservoir sizes. The longer C I line width persistence even after removing the most actively star-forming galaxies suggests its sensitivity to the large-scale reservoirs. The relationship between the C I and CO line ratios is also reflected in their respective line widths, implying a connection between the optical depth of CO and the size of the molecular gas reservoir. The presence of the $^3\Pi_{e} - ^3\Pi_{o}$ C I lines in spectral surveys makes them a valuable data set for exploring the molecular gas reservoirs in galaxies over a wide range of distances, as they offer a more direct temperature estimate and larger optical depth

In 2018, the series reconstruction problem for discrete arrangements emerged, 
addressing the challenge of restoring a discrete arrangement via its character 
tables in a polynomial time frame. Building on this foundation, our research 
expands upon this goal for discrete arrangements within the Hamming distance by 
establishing a reconstructive method employing the arrangement's character 
values, with a computational time complexity determined based on the input 
parameters and validated through a statistical experiment.

Researchers anticipate detecting gravitational waves from the gradual deformation of space-time produced by the approaching binaries within our galaxy through Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) observations. PTA analysts employ four-dimensional templates to identify these signals, however the accuracy of these templates below a certain threshold of signal-to-noise ratio is debatable. Consequently, the development of advanced methods to evaluate the precision of these templates is crucial. Furthermore, precise analysis results are typically calculated through time-domain responses of binaries to gravitational waves, evaluated at various locations within a pulsar's beam, however such approaches can be computationally expensive due to the extensive number of evaluations required. In order to enhance the analysis efficiency and provide insights into the precision of current templates, an alternative method has been developed based on a perturbative approach, suitable for the PTA context. This new method evaluates the accuracy of current templates and the analysis results, as well for the precision of the position of the sources, the Earth's spin, and the frequency of the binaries, thus providing a cost-effective solution for the analysis of real data.

We establish that in ASEP, a system with initial data represented by discrete steps, a second-class particle placed at the origin, will experience velocity fluctuations that converge to a random process with a specific distribution as time tends to infinity. This asymptotic distribution can be identified as the unique stationary distribution of an associated velocity process, which we call ASEP velocity process. ASEP velocity process is then proven to be ergodic, resulting in the stationary distribution as its unique limit for all initial conditions. This further implies that the velocity fluctuations converge to a specific double-sided random variable, whose probability density function can be determined via the asymptotic velocity distribution and initial data. Moreover, we demonstrate that the asymptotic velocity distribution is symmetric and Gaussian, leading to the conclusion that the probability density function of the velocity process is twice continuously differentiable. Consequently, the density function of the velocity process can be recovered by solving an initial value problem given by the ASEP velocity process dynamics.

Our analysis highlights the significance of considering multiple mathematical models to capture the intricate dynamics of infectious disease spread, as well as the importance of accountability in benchmarking and assessing current SARS-CoV-2 epidemic models. By reviewing key models and their limitations, we aim to encourage a more rigorous approach to evaluating and comparing existing models, as well as a greater emphasis on addressing pressing policy-related questions.

Researchers are looking at coherent atom-molecule conversions using laser light, a process that involves transforming a high degree of spin symmetry in atomic states to a more complex spin structure in molecular states. This conversion can be realized through a three-body recombination reaction that occurs when two atoms with the same properties and one displaced spin state interact and combine into a single molecule. This process, coupled with a finding from quantum chaos studies, may enable the efficient production of molecules in highly spin-polarized states, specifically in cases where two-atom scattering is closely related to a specific one-dimensional chaotic system known as the rational approximation to quantum chaotic scattering. This leads to the prediction of a specific scale of efficiency (beyond traditional recombination rates) that could be experimentally verified, potentially indicating a route to producing large quantities of highly spin-polarized molecules.

This paper introduces a new method for efficiently managing hierarchy and data updates in Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) based structural storage. The proposed technique, termed Emerge, facilitates seamless integration of incoming data with the existing graph while concurrently updating the corresponding hierarchy. Emerge identifies areas of the hierarchy that require modification and applies the necessary transformations to the graph and hierarchy simultaneously. Furthermore, Emerge facilitates reverse operations to restore the previous graph and hierarchy in case of data rollback requirements. The proposed technique addresses three key challenges in data storage: hierarchy construction, data retention, and data refactoring. The effectiveness of Emerge is demonstrated through a use case involving DNA data storage, along with experimental results showing substantial improvements in hierarchy construction time, data retention capacity, and refactoring efficiency when compared to existing approaches.

The increasing use of computational models in hydrodynamic applications is prompting for faster solutions methods. Traditional numerical methods provide accurate results but are often too slow for real-time applications. In contrast, modern machine learning techniques offer rapid solutions but with decreased precision and limited flexibility. The proposed SWDNN model bridges this precision speed tradeoff by presenting a unique combination of the shallow water equations and artificial neural networks. This novel solver features a compact size of only 1.5 million parameters and can achieve 0.25 seconds per-time-step speed. Furthermore, the model demonstrates strong performance in sequenced applications such as flood mapping with rapid water level predictions. The code for this project is available online at https://github.com/AmirTeymourian/shallow-water-DNN.

HDR photography combines multiple photos captured at various exposure levels to counterbalance digital cameras' limited dynamic range. Although HDR imaging is beneficial, selecting optimal exposure settings and processing techniques can be time-consuming and require extensive technical knowledge. This study presents a mobile HDR application, easily downloadable from the Android platform, which automates exposure selection and image processing. Utilizing a 12-image bracket with a $\pm 2$ EV range, the application automatically adjusts exposure, captures HDR images, and applies advanced processing techniques. Comparative assessments against leading HDR software and manually optimized settings reveal the mobile application's capable performance. The free mobile HDR solution enables users to experience HDR imaging on their mobile devices without technical difficulties.

Causal neural networks constitute a novel framework that applies causal graphs to govern how representations are shared and learned within a neural network. This paradigm extends the traditional neural network framework, aligning with counterfactual reasoning and learning from observational data. This paper introduces the concept of causal neural networks and explores their potential in solving pressing problems in machine learning, including dealing with confounding variables and model transfer. It also presents theoretical and practical aspects of causal neural networks, covering their mathematical foundations, implementation details, and empirical validation. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of causal neural networks in addressing confounding variables and facilitating model transfer, with performance on par with or surpassing traditional neural network baselines.

This note presents a new method for establishing the Madsen-Weiss theorem via the b-principle, specifically by proving the Madsen-Weiss theorem for orientable surfaces, and subsequently expanding to a broad class of closed surfaces.

The effectiveness of numerical solutions for cardiac mechanics models relies heavily on the efficiency of their underpinning linear solvers and matrix preconditioners. Recent studies have evaluated and compared several free and open-source solvers and preconditioners within the finite element framework, specifically for heart navigation applications. To foster further development and accuracy improvements, this study publicly releases comparison results for 12 different solvers and 13 preconditioners tried in conjunction with the PETSc library. For heart navigation, solvers that initially appeared less performant may not warrant further investigation due to their significant computational time, showing the value of previous studies' rigorous assessment. Rather than presenting novel findings, this research aims to provide a detailed report of previous results, including the wide range of preconditioners examined, for the benefit of the computational cardiology community. This includes specific data on the wide range of preconditioners examined, which may be useful for developers of cardiology software.

Standard diffusion models fail to capture the complex behavior of certain materials, like superdiffusing polynomials and biological entities, that exhibit random movements based on variable environments. These systems, which exhibit diffusion beyond the normal range, require a stochastic approach that incorporates a fractional power law element. However, even with a comprehensive stochastic model, such systems pose a significant challenge in terms of analytical solutions. In our research, we developed a mathematical model that incorporates random variables representing the fractional power law element and applied it to examine the spread of a tracer within specific geological scenarios. Our comprehensive model enables us to derive accurate equations that can be applied to a broad range of fractal domains, from simple channels to more complex porous media. Our research also involves conducting comprehensive statistical analyses to determine the reliability of our model and validate its performance across a wide range of scenarios.

Our study delves into the fundamental understanding of optical resonators, waveguides, and their interactions through linear and Kerr nonlinear coupling. By examining patterns resulting from Heisenberg's uncoupled system, we reveal the emergence of a universal framework that encompasses both phenomena, providing a comprehensive analysis of stationary and dynamic states in isolated and coupled systems. The universal theory is applied to reveal both the patterns formed within isolated optical elements and the dynamics of their coupled versions. It is essential to note that the proposed framework is inherently free from any specific reference frame, ensuring the results obtained are truly universal in nature.

A new high-resolution model is proposed to improve the visualization of turbulent flow dynamics by filling in the gaps between traditionally measured data sets. The proposed model, inspired by style transfer and image synthesis techniques, enables the creation of high-resolution, diverse images from lower-resolution ones. The developed model consists of two main components: a residual-refinement network and a global discriminator. By utilizing this model's capability to eliminate structural differences, high-resolution images can be generated from low-resolution ones by mapping them into a specific target space. The proposed framework is applied to turbulent flow simulation data, resulting in enhanced visualization capabilities and the generation of high-resolution plumes for an E-cannular flow and a wing wall flow. The model's effectiveness is evaluated in terms of PSNR and SSIM values, and the generated solutions are physically validated by computing Reynolds stresses and Nusselt numbers.

Despite notable breakthroughs in reinforcement learning, numerous significant hurdles remain when applying it to dynamic and ever-changing problems common in critical domains, including robotics and complex gameplay. Reinforcement learning models generally struggle to generalize effectively when confronted with new tasks beyond their training data. In response to this challenge, the field is seeing an increased focus on continual learning methods, and to support this research, new tools are being developed, including carefully crafted evaluation frameworks and benchmark environments. To address this need, the authors present Lifelong Learning Exploration Environment (L2Explorer), a comprehensive, open-source Python framework designed to streamline the process of evaluating and developing continual learning strategies. L2Explorer provides a comprehensive suite of evaluation tools, a modular environment design, and an accessible API to facilitate seamless integration of new continuous learning environments. The framework is accompanied by a series of rigorous experimental evaluations of numerous continual learning methods across diverse scenarios, enabling direct comparison of their performance. L2Explorer is available for public use, with source code accessible via the GitHub platform at the following location: https://github.com/NVIDIA/L2Explorer.

Interactive declarative processes can be represented by logic programs and feature procedural and declarative aspects. Procedural aspects involve action execution, while declarative aspects comprise knowledge about achievable goals. The process's effect can be viewed through a dynamic logic program that incorporates facts derived from previous actions and current goals. A key challenge arises when attempting to add new rules in response to actions, as it requires considering both past actions and current goals. A approach is proposed to address this issue by incorporating a supervisor that selects desired future states based on the process's definition, combined with an exploration component that determines optimal actions leading to preferred states. The resulting process can be viewed as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), for which solutions are available. The proposed approach is demonstrated through an air traffic control scenario and benchmark problems.
This note provides an introduction to the interplay between algebraic and geometric approaches to compactifying moduli spaces of varieties.

Determining the factors driving the slowdown of star formation in galaxies during the late stages of the universe's evolution is crucial for understanding how the cosmos transitioned from a star-forming to a quiescent state. The strong correlation between the mass of supermassive black holes and the stellar mass of bulges in galaxies suggests that black hole growth may influence this transition. However, the role of bulges in explaining the slowdown of star formation is contested, with some studies suggesting they are a primary factor and others ruling out this possibility. A new analysis addresses this debate by examining how the mass-to-light ratio of galaxies, which indicates their gas and stellar content, varies in response to bulge and black hole mass. It also considers the contribution of active galactic nuclei to the ionizing radiation that can influence the mass-tolight ratio. For analyzing these relationships and extracting physical insights, a new method is developed that separates the non-linear interactions between bulge and black hole mass. The study finds that the relationship between bulge mass and star-forming activity shows a sharp turn-on at high masses, whereas the connection between black hole mass and star-forming activity is less pronounced. If the assumption that active galactic nuclei contribute significantly to the mass-tolight ratio is removed, then the turn-on at high masses disappears. This paper explores the challenge of determining the sentiment expression for
a less commonly spoken language. Although supervised machine learning models
have achieved high accuracy in this task for widely spoken languages like
Spanish and French, they perform poorly for infrequently spoken languages like
Wu for reasons including insufficient training data. In response, this paper
develops a new approach called Cross-Linguistic Sentiment Assessment via
Multitask Training, or (CLSAT), which enables sentiment assessment for any
language. The CLSAT model combines two components: a multilingual BERT
baseline and a resource-rich positively labeled set. The model demonstrates
superior performance compared to current state-of-the-art approaches in five
less commonly spoken languages including Wu, Nepali, and others. The code
for this project has been made available on GitHub at https://github.com/zhai-lx/
CLSAT.

X-ray images contain subtle characteristics that may indicate a patient's criticality level who has been diagnosed with COVID-19. This study aims to identify these distinguishing features through convolutional neural networks, enabling potential use in rapid screening applications. By analyzing images independent of patient data, a set of important features was extracted that, when combined, can predict a patient's severe symptoms with 84% accuracy. These findings can contribute to developing low-cost, accessible screening methods for enhancing COVID-19 treatment effectiveness.

The global simplicial bundle concept, introduced by Jardine in 2006, serves as a categorical replacement for the usual notion of simplicial bundles in the context of simplicial sets. It is defined through a set of equipartition maps that satisfy certain compatibility conditions. We demonstrate that the category of global simplicial bundles has the properties of a full right simplicial adjoint to the functor that embeds the category of simplicial sets within the category of global simplicial bundles, induced by forgetting the bundle structure. As a consequence, we find that the global simplicial bundle functor is fully faithful. Furthermore, we establish that the image of the fundamental group functor can be characterized as the group of global sections of a simplicial group when the base is topologically connected.

This paper delves into the issue of erroneous positives in visual relationship detection tasks. Although significant progress has been made in recent years, detection models still struggle with a high rate of incorrect predictions. This problem is particularly pronounced for frequent relationship instances. Frequent relationships often have a high number of annotations that include background areas. As a result, detection models learn to predict these relationships from background noise, leading to excessive false positives. This research introduces a novel approach that employs a soft rejection technique to address this issue. The proposed method involves training a classifier with a low confidence threshold to identify difficult instances. Easy instances are then excluded from the training set. This leads to an increase in hard negative samples and results in the model being more cautious in its predictions. Furthermore, the proposed method includes an intuitive analysis of the problem, guidelines for dataset construction, and an innovative technique for evaluating the number of false positives. Experiments conducted on the Visual Relationship Detection Validation Set reveal a 20% reduction in false positives for frequent relationships and a 13% reduction for rare relationships. The proposed method demonstrates comparable performance to the current state-of-the-art approaches on the test set.

We've performed an in-depth analysis of five quiescent galaxies within a cluster that formed approximately 12.8 billion years ago, featuring lopsided disk structures and rapid star formation in their centers. Our study indicates these galaxies underwent a rapid star formation episode, forming low-mass stars, and possessing central bulges. Observations suggest that the formation of their bulges and the development of their asymmetrical disks occurred simultaneously, likely as a result of gas accretion that caused a shift from spiral arms to bars. This phenomenon led to altered disk morphologies and dimished asymmetry, defining a new phase of galaxy evolution. Furthermore, we discovered a relationship between the asymmetry of quiescent galaxies and their bulge-to-halo mass ratio, indicating that the disruption of galaxies contributes significantly to stellar asymptotic giant branch populations in quiescent clusters.

Recently discovered solar observations from Bolivia (5250 m above sea level) and Mexico (4600 m above sea level) reveal the presence of high-energy protons and antineutrinos associated with solar eruptions in November 2004. A comprehensive analysis of these observations, combined with satellite data from SOHO and GOES, pinpoints a large X2 flare on November 7, 2004 as the source of a high-energy particle composition change. This analysis determines the energy spectra of protons and nuclei, confirming a significant increase in high-energy backgrounds during and after the flare, and attributing changes in particle compositions to solar depth analyses. Furthermore, converting observed neutrino signals into antielectron decay modes, and analyzing them through solar radius models, reveals a distinct neutrino flux peak on November 7, 2004, correlated with the large X2 flare, and closely matched to a specific depth range within the solar core.

If a massive young star unexpectedly accelerates its rotation rate, it could be the result of a planetary interaction where a massive protoplanet migrates close to the inner edge of the disk, transferring angular momentum to the star and causing it to spin faster. We developed a model that considers the influence of a tilted disk and a solid Earth accretion process and found evidence for it in the case of a 0.9 M$_\odot$ star that quickly spins up during the early stages of its evolution. For more massive stars, our model shows that faster core contraction is necessary to match the observed rotation profiles. Additionally, we found that a positive correlation between stellar mass and the angle of the spin axis $\theta$ is inherent to the model, which aligns with observations of young open clusters. We also explored the possibility of a mysterious angular momentum source and found that if an additional 2.5\% of the star's mass is transferred to it in the form of fast-spinning solid bodies, it could explain the observed rotation patterns, though this scenario is less supported by observations.

Due to the rapid dissemination of information on social media, false news can spread very quickly, causing significant consequences, and highlighting the need for early detection methods. Current approaches to false news detection focus primarily on post-mortem analysis, relying on established facts to confirm the veracity of news, whereas emerging false news appears during the reporting period and requires more dynamic detection methods. This paper introduces a novel approach that addresses the challenge of false news identification in real-time by integrating the concept of conditional neural processes. We devise the Multimodal Meta False News Detector (MMFND), a system that learns from past experiences to quickly generalize from limited samples, incorporating the rich semantics of text and visual modalities. The MMFND comprises three components: a neural network responsible for encoding the input modalities, a neural process that produces the veracity probability distribution, and a memory storage unit for storing critical information. The text and visual encodings are shared across the neural process and memory storage, ensuring they convey identical information. The MMFND evaluates the correctness of the veracity probability distribution produced by the neural process using the squared loss and maximally expects to loss. We conduct two key experiments to evaluate MMFND: a general false news detection task and a more specific experiment focused on distinguishing truth from lie within the same experience. We compare MMFND against strong baselines, including multimodal deepfake detection models and standard false news detection classifiers, demonstrating its effectiveness in detecting emerging false news.

This research paper examines the conveyance equation, which describes how water conveys sediment within it, particularly focusing on periodic solutions. Although the conveyance equation is parabolic in nature, its bed load transport term introduces a discontinuous element causing issues with the standard application of analytic techniques. To overcome this challenge, the conveyance equation is reformed by combining the bed load transport function and a periodic function representing the periodic solutions, then analyzing its derivatives. This reformulation enables the use of harmonic analysis methods. Next, the research paper establishes the existence and uniqueness of a strong solution for the conveyance equation, followed by the proof of its regularity in BK space. Furthermore, the solution to the conveyance equation is shown to converge strongly to a unique periodic solution as the initial displacement deviates from a specific set. This research was inspired by the work of Goodman and Noh (2018), and the analysis methods employed here build upon the framework established by Goodman and Hou (2000) for the case of periodic conveyance equations.

This paper introduces a novel concept of multi-phase Golay complementary sets (MGCs) which extends the fundamental Golay complementary pairs idea to its polyphasic version. A specific category of MGCs, type I, is then defined and a method for constructing them is outlined. Specifically, a procedure is described to create sets of four sequences that form a Golay complementary pair in three phases, as well as additional sets of four sequences that are complementary in one phase. A sub-type of type I MGCs, referred to as nested type I MGCs, is also defined and an illustrative example of a double-phase Golay complementary pair is given, along with its corresponding sequence specifications.

Quantum spin transfer and tunnel coupling between valleys in silicon have been determined in bulk silicon, limiting the scalability of silicon valley quantum computing. Researchers have found that both phenomena significantly decrease in magnitude near the surface of silicon, however it has not been established if this decline persists into the atomic range. Utilizing combined scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy, the authors discovered that helium-cooled samples allow for the reduction of interface disorder, enabling the visualization of atomic-scale charge distribution in silicon surfaces. It has been found that hydrogen termination can further decrease valley coupling by approximately one order of magnitude into the atomic range, offering a promising approach for precise control of valley degrees of freedom and silicon quantum computing.

Recently, graph neural networks have emerged as a successful approach in processing complex data, leading to breakthroughs in various applications such as chemistry and social network analysis. However, the underlying principles and theoretical foundations of graph neural networks as a learning framework remain not well understood, hindering their potential potential growth. In this work, we aim to explore the intrinsic properties of graph neural networks, demonstrating that they inherently provide a consistent basis for learning inductive relationships within dynamic complex systems through the distributional hypothesis. We show that the learned representations conform to distributional hypotheses, effectively capturing the underlying structure of complex systems. Furthermore, we highlight the implications of this finding on modeling temporal complex systems, suggesting that simple graph neural networks can efficiently learn the dynamics of these systems by incorporating a self-connection in the graph, which enhances performance on real-world datasets.

This research identifies specific types of subspaces in polytopes that contribute distinct terms to the expanded versions of certain polynomial equations derived from them. A key example considers a specific class of polytopes called simple rational polytopes, for which (integer-weighted) volume equations can be established using a established method. However, these equations include extraneous terms resulting from division operations, making them complex. Our study determines the format of these subspaces, which we call delta-polytopes, and proves that all faces of a polytope that contribute terms in its volume equation are equivalent to delta-polytopes obtained from it by expanding edges.

A recent study utilizes Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) to create synthetic cerebral lesions in MRI data, with promising results, but with an optimal encoding period. Building on this research, we enhance the data encoding process by incorporating progressive encoding, achieving even more accurate lesion detection and classification in new data. Using the CenterOut validation strategy, our model accurately predicts cerebral lesions outside the training image area, with a score of 0.88, surpassing the 0.78 score from a state-of-the-art fully automated detection algorithm. With just 32 MRI images, our model can effectively create synthetic lesions in new data, with a score of 0.81, a significant improvement over the baseline score of 0.58. Our model's capability to generate precise synthetic lesions is validated through low-dimensional manifold visualization, with a compact structure reflecting complex brain lesion characteristics.

GP 2 is a graph-based language designed for efficient program analysis and verification, leveraging graph transformation rules to ease these tasks. However, determining the most effective transitions and queries to employ, given a specific problem domain, can be very challenging. In response to this difficulty, the GP 1 compiler was developed to automate the process of creating a concise memory footprint from original GP 1 programs, drawing on the GP 2 GP 1 translation framework. Building on this foundation, the Enhanced GP 2 compiler was created to address the limitations of its predecessor and the GP 2 GP 1 translation framework. The Enhanced GP 2 compiler includes multiple innovative features such as dynamic memory allocation, a revised store format, and enhanced type and array handling capabilities. These advancements permit the compiler to handle a more comprehensive range of GP 2 programs, including those featuring pointers, structures, and multi-dimensional arrays.

In recent years, due to the growth in size and complexity of datasets, dimensionality reduction techniques have become increasingly popular. One of the well-known methods in this category is the feature extraction technique, where a classifier is used in conjunction with an encoder to reduce high-dimensional data. Despite its advantages, this method has its limitations, primarily stemming from the need for separate training sessions for the encoder and the classifier. This, in turn, leads to several substantial challenges, including increased memory usage, longer training times, and the risk of overfitting. In an attempt to address these challenges, we introduce an end-to-end learning framework known as Super-Net, which seamlessly integrates both the encoder and the classifier into a single, unified structure. This innovative architecture enables direct learning from raw data without the need for pre-extraction features, allowing for automatic optimization of both the encoder and the classifier through backpropagation. We have tested and validated the efficacy of this model on three well-known datasets, and the results demonstrate significant improvements over the current state-of-the-art methods.

We have discovered an infinite family of locally finite, star-shaped graph embeddings in $\mathbb{R}^2$, generated by a specific set of rotations, which we call the twisted trapezoid formation. This class includes all 2-connected, non-contractible star-shaped graph embeddings in $\mathbb{R}^2$ that contain a pair of identical substructures placed symmetrically around a line of symmetry, as well as all embedded twisted wreath diagrams. The twisted trapezoid formation can be utilized to create a variety of graph embeddings, including all twisted wreath diagrams, knotted torus diagrams, double cover diagrams of the torus, and others.

Working with nominal data poses significant challenges when performing dimensionality reduction techniques. Since the number of categories often far exceeds the sample size, standard regularization methods may result in the selection of unnecessary categories based solely on model complexity. To address this issue, we introduce a new Group Lasso approach that accounts for the structure and importance of nominal data categories. Leveraging the underlying relationship between Fisher's exact test and the Hilbert space embedding of strings, we develop a weighted Group Lasso framework that prioritizes the selection of categories with a significant association with the target variable. Theoretical guarantees and comprehensive numerical experiments demonstrate the superior performance of this method in comparing to popular alternatives.

Pretrained language models like T0 have achieved remarkable performance on numerous
tasks, despite being trained solely on unstructured text without specific task labels.
This success prompts an exploration into whether structured knowledge can complement
unstructured data, potentially unlocking a more efficient path to general knowledge.
To investigate this hypothesis, a framework is developed to integrate structured
knowledge into a supervised manner using overlapping instances. The resulting model is
able to achieve competitive performance on five datasets, surpassing the baseline T0
model without additional structured knowledge. When paired with weak supervision, the
model is able to 14% better on Wikidata5k and 6% better on T5-DBpedia30 than T0.
5 million Wikidata entities are used to demonstrate the integration of a vast
amount of structured knowledge into the model, enabling it to accurately respond to
related questions.

Achieving a seamless visual experience and optimal map navigation requires the minimal display of aliasing effects in vector maps. This study focuses on optimizing the alias-reducing alpha values in NURBS surfaces for the specific application of line junctions on vector maps. Initially, a general approach is described for calculating optimal alpha values based on NURBS characteristics and curve features. This is followed by a more tailored analysis of line junctions, incorporating a geometric assessment to provide a precise formula for determining the ideal alpha value. A comparative evaluation of the proposed method is conducted, demonstrating its superiority in suppressing aliasing effects while maintaining computational efficiency. The findings are further validated through the implementation of the proposed algorithm in the context of vector map rendering.

In multi-channel speech enhancement, improving each individual channel signal separately can significantly reduce computational load while achieving comparable performance. This task poses a significant challenge where current state-of-the-art models, prioritizing computational efficiency while providing high quality results, are scarce. To address this gap, a dual-path convolution recurrent network called DPCRN is proposed, tailored specifically for individual channel speech enhancement. This proposed network integrates a dual-path structure and convolution recurrent modules to effectively capture both local and global temporal patterns, thereby providing a solid foundation for efficient and high-quality results. Experiments conducted on the Interspeech 2021 Challenge dataset along with WSJ and MIMIC datasets demonstrate DPCRN's superiority over existing methods in terms of both objective and subjective evaluations.

Recently introduced multi-fluid models hold promise in refining the simulation of atmospheric convection within weather and climate simulations. A dynamic framework, where fluid properties remain constant across each fluid, has been applied to a simplified vertical single-column model, in a attempt to model moist atmospheric thermodynamics. To validate the model, a two-fluid simulation of Rayleigh-B\'{e}nard convection was developed, with separate fluids assigned to ascending and descending currents. The resulting convective instability is accurately replicated with a critical Prandtl number of 22, consistent with previous research. The model's ability to capture turbulent kinetic energy in Rayleigh-B\'{e}nard convection is also examined, along with the potential implications for modeling atmospheric convection within weather and climate simulations.

We investigate three separate Jaynes-Cummings systems, labeling them system 1 through 3, with a focus on their individual qubits. Initially, the qubits in systems 1 through 3 are uncorrelated with each other and operate under independent Jaynes-Cummings interactions with their respective fields. We aim to determine authentic entanglement, defined as a non-zero and directly measured three-qubit correlation, using the Mach-Zehnder interferometry metric. Our research indicates that an authentic three-qubit correlation may form if the uncorrelated qubits, after independent interactions with their respective fields, are then put through a specific quantum measurement process known as homodyne detection. Furthermore, we establish that the magnitude of this authentic three-qubit correlation is directly proportional to the individual entanglement coefficients of the respective qubits. Consequently, if the uncorrelated qubits operate under the same Jaynes-Cummings conditions, then the magnitude of the three-qubit correlation will be in direct proportion to the square of the coefficient of the target qubit.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
organizations and individuals to track the public's emotions towards them and their rivals.
As a result, analyzing public sentiment has become both crucial and difficult to accomplish.
In this project, we gathered and manually annotated a 2000-tweet dataset from the Twitter
platform for further sentiment analysis study. With a special focus on developing a precise
long short-term memory (LSTM) based framework for sentiment classification on Twitter data.
The proposed method consists of three sequential LSTM models that are combined to achieve
accurate sentiment ratings rather than simply categorization. The proposed approach is put to
test on the assembled dataset, and the results show significant improvements over standard
classification models.

A new method developed for calculating the thermodynamic properties of a black hole, known as "shadow thermodynamics," involves analyzing the relationship between a black hole's shape, as seen in the light it blocks, and its temperature. This approach can be applied to determine the temperature spectrum of a black hole and provide insights into its holographic properties. A calculation of the temperature distribution across a linearly charged black hole was previously performed by our group. In this study, we extend this approach to a more complex type of black hole, known as a nonlinear charged black hole. This specific type of black hole possesses two distinct phases of matter separated by a boundary, known as a spinodal point, which corresponds to a critical temperature. Our analysis shows that the temperature distribution across this black hole matches the results obtained through a direct thermal analysis using its holographic surface. Moreover, our shadow thermodynamics method allows us to retrieve the total temperature by integrating the distribution, which is consistent with the entanglement temperature of its holographic surface. This indicates that the holographic property of this black hole can be determined solely from its shape, without the need for any additional input.

Quantum states can be altered through various interactions with the environment, leading to changes in both the entanglement and the Wigner function's shape. Using the Wigner-entropy threshold, we were able to detect the onset of a specific type of noise that affects both Bell-charge and Wigner non-positivity, ultimately leading to a beginning of synchronization in tomographic images. Our findings demonstrate that the Wigner-entropy criterion can indicate the onset of a particular type of noise that affects both the charge-entanglement and the Wigner function's shape, leading to a beginning of synchronization in tomographic images.

360-degree virtual travel videos offer an immersive viewing experience but present a challenge in navigating their three-dimensional space, particularly in identifying areas of interest. Current 360-degree video navigation methods either rely heavily on verbal descriptions or fail to utilize captions effectively. Leveraging captions, a readily available and rich information source, viewport forecasting can be achieved by training a caption-based neural network to predict visitor views. This network, with a simple design, utilizes captions as input and produces a predicted viewport as output, positioned in three-dimensional space. Experimental evaluations reveal that the proposed network model excels in viewport forecasting tasks, outperforming a strong baseline model by a margin of 25%. Additionally, the model demonstrates impressive generalization capabilities, achieving comparable forecasting results with those obtained during training. To further validate the proposed approach, a large-scale viewport forecasting dataset was created, consisting of 12,000 viewport pairs, which can be utilized by the research community for model training, evaluation, and modification.

Tensor network methods have effectively been utilized in recent years to handle the computational challenges associated with large-scale systems at or near thermal equilibrium. Advanced tensor network approaches, particularly those based on the Verilog-A (VGA) framework, have been successfully applied in simulating thermal correlations in various models and scenarios. However, the underlying algorithms associated with VGA often incur a significant expansion of the system's dimensions, which can result in a linear increase in computational resources and a cubic boost in memory usage. Furthermore, a serial implementation of the time-evolving block decimation algorithm within VGA can lead to an exponential growth of memory consumption, posing significant obstacles for the simulation of large systems over extended periods. In an attempt to overcome these limitations, we introduce a novel approach that leverages a local perspective and develops a range of Gaussian operators tailored for the VGA framework. These operators ensure that the dimensions of the network remain fixed throughout the simulation, eliminating the need for the time-consuming re-truncation of matrix representations. By combining this approach with an alternate implementation of the time-evolving block decimation algorithm, we significantly reduce memory consumption to a cubic proportion of the system's size. Moreover, our method allows us to simulate complex systems beyond the reach of current Gaussian tensor network capabilities.

Approximate model reduction aims to condense complex models into simplified frameworks while maintaining decoupling performance. This study focuses on restricting model reduction criteria to conform to recent decoupling standards, as outlined in reference texts. In doing so, we establish connections between conventional approximation metrics and the decoupling criteria specified in the referenced standards. A comprehensive framework is introduced to address decoupling in multi-model frameworks, incorporating examples from mechanical, electrical, and aeroservoelastic applications. The proposed approach is demonstrated through scale-oriented approximation and validation testing, with results presented for various standard test cases and a real-world aeroservoelastic scenario.

The impact of infrared renormalons in the color dipole gluon distribution's variance is being quantified, and calculations demonstrate how non-linear small-x saturation impacts shift the average value, effectively delaying the onset of infrared renormalon poles by one order of $\lambda_{\rm IR}$, in line with theoretical and meta-predictive analyses.

Research in magnetophotonic surfaces and lattices has yielded exciting possibilities for controlling and speeding up photonic processes, and there's growing interest in integrating these systems with surface plasmon polaritons. Typically, previous research has focused on creating systems that respond equally to light approaching from different angles, but there's also potential for developing orientation-sensitive systems. In a new experiment, a gold wire lattice embedded in a magnetized dielectric was studied, and it was found that its behavior changes in response to the orientation of the magnetic field. This results in the system's ability to differentiate between light approaching from normal or angled directions. The theoretical analysis of this system reveals subtle gaps that could be utilized for enhancing the interaction between surface plasmon polaritons and light within specific frequency ranges.

Recent advances in neural network adversarial attacks and defenses rely heavily on benchmark datasets created by individual researchers. Although these datasets are commonly used for performance evaluation and testing, they have limited representation due to their source. In this paper, a novel approach is introduced that enables the quality assessment of individual test datasets without access to the comprehensive training datasets. The proposed method involves training a neural network to make classification decisions on a subset of the comprehensive data, with the remaining data serving as a test set. The resulting model is then used as a benchmark for evaluating the quality of individual test datasets. The assessment results show that the proposed method performs comparably to training a neural network on the comprehensive data, with a significant reduction in training data requirements. In particular, the proposed method can effectively assess the quality of individual test datasets even when they contain a thousand classes, which is infeasible for conventional neural network training. Experiments conducted on the ADULT classification task demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in evaluating the quality of individual test datasets under the constraint of limited data.

Researchers have observed the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_L$ decay mode for the first time, and have also gathered evidence for the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_L$ decay mode, utilizing a 3.0 $\text{fb}^{-1}$ dataset of $pp$ collisions collected at 7 and 8 TeV center-of-mass energies by the LHCb. The branching fractions for these decays are calculated as follows: The $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 \bar{K}^0$ branching fraction is estimated at (4.3±0.5±0.3±0.3±0.6) ×10^-4, and the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} \bar{K}^0$ branching fraction is estimated at (2.8±1.0±0.3±0.2±0.4) ×10^-4, with the given uncertainties stemming from various sources.

Given a module $M$ that is free of submodules' multiplicities and a lattice $\Lambda_M$ representing the submodule inclusion relationships, we develop an algorithm to construct the lattice of submodules of $M$. The input for this construction consists of three main components: a set of basic submodules $S_0$ forming a basis for $M$, a set of independent submodules $I_1$ generated from Serre's relations, and the lattice $\Lambda_{I_1}$ defining the inclusion relationships among $I_1$. The output is the lattice $\Lambda_M$ describing the relationship structure among all submodules of $M$. Additionally, a modification of the algorithm is introduced to accommodate modules $M$ with known composition series.

Recent advances in student-teacher models and co-learning techniques have facilitated the incorporation of multiple observers in various applications. However, incorporating expert observations is often based on the assumption that expert observations are readily available, which can create a problem in real-world scenarios. This study investigates a more challenging scenario in which the student must learn from observations of other students without access to the corresponding expert observations. We introduce the concept of co-observation learning to address this issue and present a novel framework based on a teacher-student model. In this framework, students observe other students that have been trained on the same dataset and then learn from those observations to refine their performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework with multiple network co-observation learning, which involves multiple students with different network configurations observing each other, and present experimental results showing significant performance gains over single observation learning and traditional teacher-student models.

This paper proposes a metric function that yields a more efficient computation of pulse-addition codes (PACs), enabling faster determination of whether a signal lies within a code's distance threshold. Originally, defining the PAC distance entailed solving an NP-hard problem; however, we present an alternative framework utilizing the $l_1$ norm and involving a simpler calculation that leverages the set of a signal's constituent pulses. Furthermore, we introduce pulse-addition code (PAC) versions, analogous to duplicate versions of codes, which replicate the original code's structure around a signal of varying amplitude.

Post-translation editing (TE) indicates a stage following translation where the output is refined for greater accuracy. Since TE resembles a form of post-text generation editing, training models on TE datasets can enhance neural machine translation (NMT) models by teaching them to correct their own mistakes. Nonetheless, widespread TE datasets are hard to find, and many existing methods focus mainly on utilizing TE for model fine-tuning, neglecting the potential of NMT to handle complex action spaces. In response, this study introduces a novel approach, action-value function-based reinforcement learning, which leverages TE for training standard NMT models by introducing a controlled action space. Unlike selective TE actions that correct specific words, our proposed method encourages the NMT model to produce more fluent first drafts by exploring all possible TE actions. We evaluate this approach using three diverse TE datasets and find it boosts the translation quality automatically, confirming the potential of NMT to handle extensive action spaces. Furthermore, our analysis uncovers valuable insights into action density, action utility, and their interconnected nature, presenting a way forward for further research.

The study of open quantum systems under periodic driving forces is highly captivating and can exhibit non-rigorous, quasi-periodic behavior in their quantum states. In this study, we conducted accurate theoretical calculations of a periodically driven qubit in a marked environment, comparing the results to rigorous simulations through DMITA. The theory was further developed to accommodate periodic driving in the Redfield approach, enabling the analysis of large systems through a quasi-chaotic extension of the theory, referred to as QSA. Disparities between the two descriptions emerged, indicating that the system may not be at a steady-state equilibrium and instead is in a non-equilibrium state. This conclusion is supported by an observed of a beat pattern in the time-dependent spectral lineshapes, indicative of constant energy exchange between the system and the surrounding environment.

We explore how several key biharmonic operator compositions lead to specific simplifications within the Euclidean space, ultimately resulting from the repeated application of the Laplace operator. Key biharmonic operator combinations, including those involving the Ricci operator, are examined in detail.

A real number d is classified as normally natural if its binary representation contains an infinite sequence of ones following any segment of zeros. The goal of this study is to examine numbers of this nature within the context of a specific transformation called the standard map, particularly in regards to its periodic points and its phase space. We will investigate how the standard map affects normally natural numbers when applied both directly and indirectly, and we will determine the parameters under which this map generates periodic points that identify normally natural sets. We will also establish a connection between the standard map and a second transformation called the double standard map, which enables us to tackle the task of finding periodic points that correspond to rational numbers in their most reduced form.

MongoDB, a popular NoSQL document-oriented database, offers three levels of
transactional consistency controls, including atomic operations, multi-document
transactions and two variants of embedded transactions within the MongoDB 3.6
release. Although providing extensive flexibility, the lack of a built-in mechanism
for automatically detecting inconsistencies within these transactions poses a
challenge. To address this issue, a method is proposed to validate the integrity of
MongoDB transactions utilizing three components: (1) a query language named Quiver,
(2) a validation framework named Vesta, and (3) a set of predefined integrity rules
defined using a graph-based approach. Furthermore, the proposed method is tested
on real-world datasets extracted from various applications.

Using the elementary symmetric polynomial basis, we re-express the chromatic symmetric polynomials in terms of the power sum symmetric polynomials. This conversion yields a straightforward proof of the $e$-positivity of these polynomials, demonstrating that each symmetric polynomial can be represented as a non-negative integer combination of symmetric powers of the standard symmetric polynomial. Additionally, a connection to the inverse Kostka matrix is established, showing that the coefficients of these power sum expansions correspond to the entries of the inverse Kostka matrix. This implies that the entries of the inverse Kostka matrix are composed of the moments of the Gaussian free field, which can be confirmed via a direct computation.

A recently introduced geometric theory, revealing that any high-dimensional shape can be broken down into its most fundamental components through a process called topological decomposition, is applied to a complex problem involving a specific type of triangular-based S-shaped arrangement, known as a net of triads. This specific net of triads possesses a higher dimensionality that necessitates its high-dimensional representation, thereby allowing for the accommodation of various non-trivial dynamics within a lower-dimensional space without sacrificing its inherent triangular feature. Triangular-based S-shaped arrangements of this nature are observed in nanoscale assemblies composed of magnetic molecules exhibiting triangular interactions, where the geometry plays a crucial role in determining the dynamics of spin reversal. The introduction of a specific non-linear parameter in the assemblies' dynamics allows for the emergence of complex patterns such as spin reversal, triangulation, and shape transformation. The underlying dynamics can be explained by a simple non-linear equation derived from a combination of FHN and Ginzburg-Landau equations, which forms the basis for numerical simulations including the simulation of assemblies with both pairwise and triangular interactions, where the assemblies' configurations are reconstructed from the solutions of the non-linear equation.

The solar wind surrounding Earth and other planets is influenced by the solar atmosphere's extended magnetic field. This bound plasma, known as the solar breeze, carries energy away from the sun. Researchers have yet to map the energy transferred to the solar breeze across the extraterrestrial surface due to the limited reach of this bound plasma. The Parker Solar Probe, in its interior one AU, has the chance to gauge the energy the solar breeze carries as it steers towards Earth. New data from the probe's high-resolution cameras and wind meters allow a first look at the energy the solar breeze transports as it journeys towards our planet. Findings show the solar breeze's energy fades at a rate of 0.068 watts per square meter per astronomical unit and supports previous theories that solar wind acceleration occurs closer to the sun than previously believed.

Thanks to speech-emotion recognition technology, computers can gain a more human-like understanding of the underlying sentiments and feelings conveyed through spoken language. Nonetheless, making this technology practical for widespread use outside of laboratory settings requires enhancing the algorithm's ability to adapt to new environments and improve the efficacy of training data utilization. In response to these challenges, researchers have experimentally proven the effectiveness of a novel practical solution for adapting DRL in conjunction with limited labeled data, resulting in a 14% improvement in accuracy and enabling successful applications in real-world environments.

Researchers explored a new model of an intense expanding shock wave within a homogeneous, endlessly growing cosmos, characterized by a constant speed that surpasses the speed of light, as observed from a fixed external frame of reference. This model includes the formation of a spherical cavity at the shock wave's center. Through the use of a Lorentz transformation, a constant acceleration was applied to the expanding shock wave reference frame. Two distinct cases emerged: a shock wave with a decelerating cavity (when alpha > 1) and a shock wave with a accelerating cavity (when alpha < 1), where alpha represents the ratio of the shock wave's speed to the speed of light. Various quantities such as the shock front distance, the cavity's radius, the density and pressure within the shock wave, were calculated for both scenarios.

Using $B_s^0\rightarrow D_s^{*-}\mu^+\nu_{\mu}$ events, QCD approaches were tested to determine their suitability for fitting for $|V_{ts}|$ and $|V_{td}|$. The main focus was on the $q^2$ dependence of hadron form factors, particularly whether they should be treated as semi-animally or fully based on quark levels. Four fit methods were examined to determine their impact on $|V_{ts}|$ and $|V_{td}|$ estimates. The study evaluated the likelihood of different form factor models and parameters in relation to $|V_{ts}|$ and $|V_{td}|$, with an eye towards future experiments where accurate form factor predictions will be crucial.

A key concept in the development of integrable systems and Riemann-Hilbert problems is the basis of specialized orthogonal polynomial sets, often associated with classical special functions. Building upon the foundation of classical orthogonal polynomials, a general framework is introduced that incorporates higher-order variants, specifically the classical classical classical orthogonal polynomials of multiple variables. The proposed framework utilizes a modified version of the steepest descent method to transform a specific scalar integral operator into a form that is solvable through a standard assembly of root systems. This involves examining the properties of a special set of transformed discrete operators, which can be shown to exhibit positive semi-definite spectra. The study of one-dimensional Schrödinger operators within this context allows for a transformation of the potential $v(x)$ into a new potential $\tilde{v}(x)$ through a change of variables, which in turn leads to the formation of monodromy-free Toda tachyon, notably including the generalized Hermite, Laguerre, and Jacobi polynomials sets. The development of a transformation that maps the potential $\tilde{v}(x)$ back to the original potential $v(x)$ is achieved through the integration of a specific scalar integral operator, which can be solved through the analysis of root systems. This in turn enables the recovery of the original potential $v(x)$ through a discrete assembly of the spectral parameters, which can be shown to exhibit positive semi-definite spectra.
